tasks.title: Ship the recoverable native Input vertical
tasks.objective: Implement one public short-lived native Input operation whose exact result can be recovered after response loss within the same daemon incarnation without another PTY write.
tasks.outcome: Rust clients can retain one instance-bound Input operation, reconnect, recover its exact applied byte range, and fail closed on conflict, stale cursor, ambiguous write, or daemon replacement.
acceptance: The next protocol generation advertises one random daemon-incarnation identity and defines a bounded opaque Input operation key, exact Run and non-empty bytes, expected input byte cursor, exact applied half-open byte range, and typed instance, conflict, and cursor failures.

The existing native Input owner is the only physical writer and orders instance fence, exact retained-key recovery or conflict, missing-key cursor validation, and physical write; matching retry returns the original range without mutation.
The per-Run completed-result ledger is bounded by entry count and retained request bytes; eviction cannot turn a stale operation into a new write because its expected cursor fails closed.

Every successful legacy or recoverable native Input advances the same applied-input cursor; partial or ambiguous write produces no applied range, consumes or fences the operation, and preserves the existing poisoned-lane safety boundary.

One real-PTY public test combines response loss, fresh-client reconnect, exact-result recovery, and child-side proof that bytes were written once; focused owner tests cover conflict, eviction, empty input, and ambiguous write, while a live second-daemon test proves instance rejection before mutation.

AttachmentCommandId remains connection-local correlation. No durable Resize, Stop Tree, Signal, SSH, release, general operation framework, Agent, Message, Delivery, ACK, Reply, Task, DAG, or UI-timeline semantics are added.

verification.proves: The native owner algebra and real-PTY response-loss vertical pass.
The Rust public client retains instance-bound operation identity and validates exact results.

tasks.title: Expose TypeScript recoverable Input parity
tasks.objective: Expose the same instance-bound recoverable Input operation through the generated TypeScript wire contract and dependency-free SDK without creating a second semantic implementation.
tasks.outcome: A fresh SDK client can retry a caller-retained operation after response loss and receive the original applied byte range while runtime validation rejects malformed or mismatched results.
acceptance: Rust protocol types remain the wire-shape SSOT; generated TypeScript declarations, runtime validation, exports, and SDK client API carry the original daemon instance, operation key, Run, expected cursor, exact bytes, and applied range.
The SDK never replaces an operation's retained daemon instance with a new handshake value and never represents bytes_applied as target acknowledgement or reply.

One focused wrong-case group covers new frame validation and typed failures, and one real-daemon SDK test proves fresh-client result recovery; Rust tests remain the non-duplication, conflict, eviction, and instance-fence authority.
Existing attachment Input behavior and public unknown disposition remain unchanged.

verification.proves: SDK runtime validation, client behavior, and focused real-daemon parity pass.

tasks.title: Review and close the bounded Input contract
tasks.objective: Independently review the shipped Input owner boundary and close the Feature with proportionate public evidence and current documentation.
tasks.outcome: The recoverable Input claim is source-bound, has no open P0 or P1 defect in its finite scope, and does not keep adjacent control or release work open.
acceptance: Independent read-only review covers correctness, owner and lock boundaries, partial-write disposition, bounded resources, protocol and SDK parity, naming, complexity, and product drift for this Input vertical only.

Any P0 or P1 within the shipped claim receives a deterministic regression and re-review; adjacent Stop, Resize, Signal, SSH, release, coverage, tmux, and performance findings are routed without expanding this Feature.
Protocol, architecture, SDK, and test documentation state that bytes_applied proves only the daemon-owned PTY boundary and that cross-daemon exactly-once and semantic acknowledgement are unsupported.
A clean exact revision passes the ordinary repository Gate once; no soak, platform matrix, metrics sink, coverage campaign, or general qualification framework is required for closure.

verification.proves: Formatting, static analysis, Rust and TypeScript contracts, public E2E behavior, and repository regressions pass together.
The bounded independent review, finding dispositions, exact revision, and residual limits are auditable.
